items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: For one week, Buster Bailey and I got together on the Kirby book which I must admit was one of the toughest that I ever had to tackle.

ctx.x: In those days, we did not have musical papers, and only a few of the guys bought records. The recording of "Money Blues" with Armstrong's solo on it, was the first Fletcher Henderson recording I had heard. Perhaps that is why there were quite a lot of players who were not influenced by Louis Armstrong; For instance, the trumpet player Frankie Newton, who joined Lloyd Scott's orchestra the same time as I, was more influenced by Bix Beidebeck, as was another trumpet player, whose name was Hicks, who was in the band…

I enjoyed Fletcher's band and eventually found out the names of the musicians and especially the soloists such as Charlie "Big" Green, trombone. Joe Smith and Armstrong, Buster Bailey, and Coleman Hawkins-who was the tenor sax and bass saxophone player that could swing a band into bad health. You could hear his sax cutting through when the whole band was giving everything they had ensemble.

Then there were Henderson records with Armstrong and Joe Smith and these were somthing to write home about, except that I was at home! But they were great, Armstrong and Joe Smith as a team. Suddenly there were records of Louis Armstrong and his Hot Five and I learned that Louis had left Fletcher and gone back to Chicago where he had been before joining Fletcher.
